feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with the target title. Writing is polished overall, but the document is slightly repetitive and would be stronger with sharper outcomes, tighter structure, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at one organization plus current consulting work signal trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Strong scope and relevance: Drupal migration, analytics stack, studio buildout, AI-enabled search, and cross-channel leadership show modern, high-value capability.  
- Generally strong writing: concise, professional tone with good use of specifics such as “10,000+ page website” and “3.5 million annual page views.”

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable impact beyond scope: include results like traffic growth, email performance, engagement gains, cost savings, team size, budget size, or project outcomes.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; these sections overlap and dilute impact. Consolidating would improve structure and scannability.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; choose one punctuation style for lists (“workflows and systems” vs. “workflows, systems”); “French (A2/Learning)” is slightly awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “French (basic working proficiency).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive opening, tighter phrasing, and slightly more emphasis on recent enterprise-scale web and governance work.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Lead with current value proposition: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with grouped language to improve flow and reduce repetition.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading cross-channel content, web, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable complex communications operations. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and “platform modernization” are repeated in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; keep the intro high-level.
- “Workflows and systems” also appears elsewhere, so avoid adding more operational detail here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing leadership-level strengths will make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership”; “Web & CMS administration” → “Web platform governance & CMS management.”
- Group related items to reduce repetition and improve flow: strategy/governance, content/workflows, analytics, stakeholder leadership, multimedia.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout for consistency.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & platform transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform governance & CMS management • Editorial operations & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Systems architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder & cross-functional leadership • Advocacy, policy & member communications • Multimedia, video & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills.
- Several items repeat the header and Topline Skills almost verbatim; consider shortening or removing this section if space is tight.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope and good alignment to your headline, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around 3–5 high-impact outcomes and distinguish it from your NACo leadership role by emphasizing consulting, build work, and AI/search delivery.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one outcome-focused line; e.g., “Built cross-channel workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Reframe technical bullets to show business value: “Developed Drupal campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and member toolkits that improved campaign launch speed and content reuse.”
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages supported, users, launch timelines reduced, toolkit downloads, search success, engagement lift, or publishing efficiency gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, analytics, workflows” overlaps with Director of Digital Media; keep this entry more execution- and consulting-focused.
- AI-enabled search also appears in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same description verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be stronger if the opening were tighter and the bullets emphasized outcomes, team/budget scope, and what changed under your leadership.

Suggested edit
- Replace the broad opener with a sharper scope statement: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget oversight.”
- Tighten and front-load impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible for channels/studio/analytics: subscriber growth, engagement rates, production cost savings, reporting speed, adoption, or decision-making improvements.
- Use stronger result-oriented phrasing in the final bullets, e.g., “Established governance and publishing standards that improved cross-department coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Email/social/video operations overlap with the prior NACo role; in this entry, emphasize enterprise leadership, platform modernization, analytics, governance, and budget ownership.
- “Built first in-house video studio” may overlap with footer project examples; keep this version strategic and outcome-focused.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later NACo role and the earlier digital media role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, editorial operations, and channel growth before the director-level strategy work.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and cross-team editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders” and “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Add measurable operational impact if available: newsletter open/click growth, video cadence/views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Replace softer phrasing like “helped improve” with ownership language: “Standardized digital publishing workflows and strengthened editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; keep this version focused on scaling/operationalizing it.
- Website/email/social oversight overlaps with the 2022–2024 director role; avoid strategy/governance language here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership

- Audience-focused content planning

- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications

- If space allows, consider “enterprise web and content governance” to connect more directly to your most recent work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” repeat language already used in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also overlaps with multiple recent experience bullets; keep only if this section needs a leadership signal.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

- WordPress
- SharePoint

- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills item, make it more selective, grouped, and tied to the most recent/highest-impact work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped capability themes, e.g.: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages • Enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal/CMS modernization/AI-enabled search first, since those are most supported by recent roles and projects.
- Consider replacing “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based workflow systems” for clearer business value.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one proof point tied to recent work, e.g. “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “AI-enabled legislative search.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let Technical + IT hold the full tool list.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase in both places.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT,” so this version should emphasize strategic application and outcomes, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics infrastructure (GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI) • User behavior insights (Microsoft Clarity) • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership reporting • SEO and digital performance analysis”
- Group tools in parentheses to reduce listiness and improve scanability.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Decision-ready reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work: “analytics infrastructure for enterprise web modernization” or “reporting for 10,000+ page, 3.5M annual page-view platform.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and leave full tool inventory below.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader analytics language unless differentiated.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent leadership-level capabilities rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward scope and delivery: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to align with the NACo studio build and in-house capacity expansion.

- If space allows, make it more outcome-oriented: “Studio buildout and operations” or “Recurring advocacy video and event production” ties better to recent experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section overlaps with Core Competencies: “Multimedia production and livestream operations.”
- “Studio operations” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” may also echo Work Experience bullets about building the in-house studio and event production capacity.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. Use this space to signal depth and recency—especially Drupal—rather than repeat generic CMS names.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites, modular content)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint / Power Pages** • **GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add proficiency context instead of just names: **Drupal 10/enterprise CMS** rather than plain “Drupal.”
- Consider tightening to the platforms you’ve clearly used in recent roles; if GitHub Pages was minor, remove it.
- Optional rewrite: **Drupal (enterprise sites, migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider deleting one section or making this one more specific.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t restate it here unless tied to a platform.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, and automation work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/refocus toward execution: “Front-End & Technical Implementation” or “Development & Deployment Tools.”
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • REST/API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions CI/CD”
- If accurate, add scope or outcomes in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., GTM for analytics deployment, Workers for edge logic, GitHub Actions for deployment automation.
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; they date the section without adding value.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear under Topline Skills; keep them in one place or make this version more tool-specific.
- “Workflow automation” is covered elsewhere; avoid implying the same capability here unless tied to GitHub Actions or Workers.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere, so tighten and frame around business use.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Group by function for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show depth: **Built and managed workflow systems in Airtable, Power Automate and Zapier; coordinated delivery in Jira, Asana and Trello**
- Consider dropping one lower-value tool if space is tight; keep the platforms most relevant to recent enterprise digital operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing
- Slack/Teams are common baseline tools; they add less value than automation platforms unless tied to workflow use

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of capability. It would be stronger if framed around campaign/email operations and aligned to the seniority shown in recent NACo work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms** for clearer positioning.
- Reorder by likely depth/relevance: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**.
- If accurate, add functional context instead of only product names, e.g. **Higher Logic (newsletter operations, audience segmentation) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey orchestration, CRM-linked campaigns) • Mailchimp (campaign deployment)**.
- If one platform was only lightly used, consider dropping it to keep the list credible and focused.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with work experience bullets about leading email newsletters; avoid repeating “email strategy/operations” elsewhere in the skills section.
- “Engagement” is broad; don’t imply community platform ownership unless Higher Logic included that scope.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, platform refresh support, and hands-on production.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted through two digital roles while helping build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize day-to-day workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make contributions concrete: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand the organization’s in-house communications capacity.”
- Tighten management language: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised daily work of a digital media associate.”
- Add metrics if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this item focused on launching/establishing the format, not expanding it.
- Avoid repeating governance/workflow language already used more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes so it complements—rather than repeats—your later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize ownership and firsts: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Split multimedia work into a stronger impact statement: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support member communications and policy storytelling.”
- Make the podcast launch the anchor achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add one measurable result: number of episodes, audience/downloads, internal stakeholders supported, or projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad phrases like “digital content production and multimedia materials,” which overlap with later digital media roles unless tied to a distinct early-career contribution.
- Don’t overstate strategic leadership here; later roles already show progression into enterprise digital ownership.
